skill.name: sharp-edges
skill.description: Find error-prone API usage and dangerous configuration choices before they cause security or reliability issues.
skill.summary: Guides focused reviews of risky APIs, unsafe defaults, and configuration sharp edges.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only static findings are GitHub source links in SKILL.md, and both are documentation references. No executable code, prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or business-logic abuse was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: The URL is a front matter source link to a GitHub repository, not an instruction to fetch data or contact a service. The skill is prompt-only and contains no executable network behavior.
The URL appears in a Resources section as documentation for the skill source. It does not request network access, transmit data, or alter agent behavior.

content.value_statement: Risky APIs and unsafe defaults can hide reliability and security problems. This skill guides focused review of dangerous usage patterns and configuration choices.
actual_capabilities: Reviews API usage for error-prone patterns and unclear failure modes.
Identifies dangerous defaults and settings that bypass security controls.
Assesses risk from resource management, concurrency, timing, and error handling issues.
Supports code, configuration, and documentation review workflows.
Recommends safer alternatives and clearer documentation when risks are found.
limitations: It does not run scanners or verify findings against live systems.
It depends on the files, context, and goals supplied by the reviewer.
It cannot prove that an API or configuration is safe in every environment.
It may need domain-specific input for specialized platforms or frameworks.

use_cases.title: Pre-merge Security Review
use_cases.description: Review risky API calls and configuration changes before they reach production.

use_cases.title: Production Configuration Audit
use_cases.description: Find unsafe defaults, bypass settings, and reliability risks in service configuration files.

use_cases.title: Developer Documentation Review
use_cases.description: Improve examples and warnings so teams avoid dangerous usage patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Configuration
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one configuration file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the sharp-edges skill to review this configuration. Identify dangerous defaults, bypass settings, reliability risks, and safer alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Find Risky API Usage
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of API calls in source files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the sharp-edges skill to inspect these API calls. Focus on confusing parameters, hidden failure modes, resource cleanup, timing issues, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Pull Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a change set before merge.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the sharp-edges skill to review this pull request. List each risky API or configuration change, explain impact, and suggest a safer implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Sharp Edges Register
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the sharp-edges skill to create a project risk register. Group findings by API misuse, dangerous configuration, reliability risk, and documentation gap.

output_examples.input: Review this service configuration for dangerous defaults before deployment.
output_examples.output: Flags disabled authentication, broad cross-origin access, weak timeout settings, and safer production defaults to evaluate.

output_examples.input: Analyze this API wrapper for sharp edges.
output_examples.output: Highlights confusing parameter order, missing cleanup on failure, unclear errors, and a safer wrapper design.

output_examples.input: Check our service documentation for risky guidance.
output_examples.output: Identifies missing warnings, examples that bypass validation, and clearer guidance for safe usage.

best_practices: Provide the relevant API calls, configuration files, and deployment context together.
Ask for severity, impact, and safer alternatives for each finding.
Validate recommendations with maintainers who understand the runtime environment.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the output as proof that a system is secure.
Do not review isolated snippets when configuration depends on environment settings.
Do not ignore low-severity sharp edges that appear across many services.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews API usage, configuration choices, and documentation for risky patterns and unsafe defaults.

faq.question: Does it execute code or run scanners?
faq.answer: No. It is a prompt-only review guide and does not execute code or run external tools.

faq.question: Can it replace a security audit?
faq.answer: No. It helps focus review, but human validation and project-specific testing remain necessary.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Relevant source files, configuration files, deployment assumptions, and known reliability or security goals work best.

faq.question: How should teams use the results?
faq.answer: Teams should prioritize confirmed risks, choose safer defaults, and document accepted exceptions.
